name: Risco Caido and the Sacred Mountains of Gran Canaria Cultural Landscape
description: In the rugged volcanic heart of Gran Canaria, this landscape of cliffs, ravines and rock pinnacles is dotted with caves that the island's pre-Hispanic inhabitants carved into the stone as homes, grain stores and water cisterns. Two sacred sites, Risco Caído and Roque Bentayga, were places of seasonal ceremony, possibly tied to the stars and Mother Earth. Visitors can see how an isolated island culture lived for some 1,400 years.
